paragraphs: I'm applying for the Security Engineer (Blue Team) role in Hawthorne. Building the detection tooling and data pipelines that let a SOC catch real adversaries, in an environment that launches rockets, is the defensive work I most want to do. I finished my B.S. in Computer Science at UC Irvine, specializing in Networked Systems, I'm local to Irvine/Orange County, and I'm a U.S. citizen.

I write Python and Node.js regularly, and I've worked with ETL and data-engineering pipelines. I also built and operate CommunicAI, an AI-powered iOS app on the App Store running on Gemini Flash and Google Cloud, and I own its security. My server-authoritative Cloud Functions enforce authentication, input validation and rate limiting, and they verify Apple receipts server-side to catch subscription fraud. I wrote role-based access-control rules that block IDOR, privilege escalation and message spoofing, and 36 adversarial unit tests try to break them. Thinking like an attacker to find where a control fails is the habit I'd bring to detection engineering and adversary emulation.

On the offensive side, I've used Wireshark and Burp Suite in labs to study MITM, ARP poisoning, DNS spoofing, SQL injection and XSS, including what each attack leaves behind. I haven't run a SIEM or worked an incident professionally yet. I'm studying for the CompTIA Security+ exam in January, and I learn quickly under pressure. As captain of UC Irvine's NCAA Division I track and field team, I'm used to long days and weekend commitments.
I'd welcome the chance to help the Blue Team close visibility gaps, and I'm ready to work fully on-site, including extended hours when the mission needs it.
